Site: OYO-2 PV PLANT (LAT 8.10N, LON 3.35E)
Date of work: 2024-09-18
Technician: T.O. (Tunde Okafor) & J.B. (James Bello)
Time on site: 08:00 – 16:30 WAT (8h 30m)

Work performed:
Detailed inspection of Turbine Blade TB-12. Turbine Blade TB-12 has inspection_date 2024-09-18. Record status: current. This was the scheduled quarterly visual and ultrasonic inspection of the blade, which is the longest blade on the site at 58m. We used the drone for the initial visual sweep, then did a rope-access check on the leading edge and the tip section where we had previously noted some leading-edge erosion back in the March inspection (FSR-2024-0312).

Scope of work:
1. Drone sweep of the full blade surface – both the pressure side and suction side. Got high-resolution photos of the entire surface. The drone footage was saved to the site server under the usual folder structure.
2. Visual inspection of the leading edge from the root to the tip using rope access. Focused on the erosion areas identified in March. The erosion has progressed slightly – the deepest pits are now about 2-3mm deep, up from 1-2mm in March. Still within acceptable limits but I recommend we plan for leading-edge protection tape application during the next major service window, likely Q1 2025.
3. Ultrasonic thickness testing at 12 points along the blade. All readings are within spec – the minimum thickness we found was 4.2mm at the trailing edge near the 40m mark, which is still above the 3.5mm minimum specified by the manufacturer.
4. Checked the lightning protection system on the blade. Verified continuity from the tip receptor to the root grounding strap. Resistance reading was 0.4 ohms, well within the 1-ohm limit.
5. Inspected the root bolts and the pitch bearing interface. All bolts were properly torqued (checked with torque wrench, all within spec). No signs of fretting or corrosion at the bolt heads.
6. Checked the vortex generators on the outer third of the blade. Found two missing vortex generators – one at the 44m mark on the suction side and one at the 51m mark on the pressure side. These are small plastic fins that help control airflow. Their loss won't cause any immediate issues but should be replaced to maintain optimal performance. I've ordered replacements through the normal parts channel.

Asset conditions:
- TB-12 blade: Good overall. Minor leading-edge erosion, two missing vortex generators.
- Lightning protection: Good.
- Root bolts: Good.
- Ultrasonic thickness: All within spec.

Parts replaced:
- None (no parts replaced during this inspection).

Time on site includes 1 hour for lunch and 30 minutes for the pre-work safety briefing and rope-access equipment setup. The wind was light (8-12 m/s) so the blade was in the ideal position for the rope access work.

Weather: Clear, sunny, max temp 35°C. Light wind.

Signatures: T.O., J.B.

Checked the gearbox oil level and took a sample for lab analysis. Oil color was normal, no metallic particles visible. Checked the hydraulic system pressure – 180 bar, within spec. Checked the nacelle for any oil leaks – found a small seep at the high-speed shaft seal. It's a minor weep, not a drip. I cleaned the area and will monitor it on the next visit. Noted for the monthly report.
3. TB-8: Checked the blade pitch system. The pitch accumulator pressure was low (130 bar vs. spec of 150 bar). I recharged the accumulator to 150 bar. Checked for leaks in the pitch lines – found none. The accumulator may need replacement in the coming months if it loses pressure again. Checked the blade root bolts – all torqued to spec. Checked the oil level in the gearbox – normal.
4. Both turbines: Checked the lightning protection systems. All readings were within spec (resistance < 1 ohm). Checked the emergency stop function on both turbines – tested and confirmed working.

FIELD SERVICE REPORT – FSR-2024-0918
Site: OYO-2 PV PLANT (LAT 8.10N, LON 3.35E)
Date of work: 2024-09-18
Technician: T.O. (Tunde Okafor) & J.B. (James Bello)
Time on site: 08:00 – 16:30 WAT (8h 30m)

Work performed:
Detailed inspection of Turbine Blade TB-12. Turbine Blade TB-12 has inspection_date 2024-09-18. Record status: current. This was the scheduled quarterly visual and ultrasonic inspection of the blade, which is the longest blade on the site at 58m. We used the drone for the initial visual sweep, then did a rope-access check on the leading edge and the tip section where we had previously noted some leading-edge erosion back in the March inspection (FSR-2024-0312).

Scope of work:
1. Drone sweep of the full blade surface – both the pressure side and suction side. Got high-resolution photos of the entire surface. The drone footage was saved to the site server under the usual folder structure.
2. Visual inspection of the leading edge from the root to the tip using rope access. Focused on the erosion areas identified in March. The erosion has progressed slightly – the deepest pits are now about 2-3mm deep, up from 1-2mm in March. Still within acceptable limits but I recommend we plan for leading-edge protection tape application during the next major service window, likely Q1 2025.
3. Ultrasonic thickness testing at 12 points along the blade. All readings are within spec – the minimum thickness we found was 4.2mm at the trailing edge near the 40m mark, which is still above the 3.5mm minimum specified by the manufacturer.
4. Checked the lightning protection system on the blade. Verified continuity from the tip receptor to the root grounding strap. Resistance reading was 0.4 ohms, well within the 1-ohm limit.
5. Inspected the root bolts and the pitch bearing interface. All bolts were properly torqued (checked with torque wrench, all within spec). No signs of fretting or corrosion at the bolt heads.
6. Checked the vortex generators on the outer third of the blade. Found two missing vortex generators – one at the 44m mark on the suction side and one at the 51m mark on the pressure side. These are small plastic fins that help control airflow. Their loss won't cause any immediate issues but should be replaced to maintain optimal performance. I've ordered replacements through the normal parts channel.

Asset conditions:
- TB-12 blade: Good overall. Minor leading-edge erosion, two missing vortex generators.
- Lightning protection: Good.
- Root bolts: Good.
- Ultrasonic thickness: All within spec.

Parts replaced:
- None (no parts replaced during this inspection).

Time on site includes 1 hour for lunch and 30 minutes for the pre-work safety briefing and rope-access equipment setup. The wind was light (8-12 m/s) so the blade was in the ideal position for the rope access work.

3. Inspected the DC cabling from SCB-7 to INV-4. Found some cable ties that had come loose near the trench entry point. Re-secured them. No visible damage to the cable jacket.
